app.name: wacli
app.one_liner: A third-party WhatsApp CLI tool that enables local message sync, offline search, and programmatic messaging via the WhatsApp Web protocol.

screens.name: Main CLI Interface
screens.purpose: Provide command-line access to WhatsApp features including auth, sync, message listing/searching, sending, and group management.

rust_commands.name: auth
rust_commands.purpose: Initiate QR code login and bootstrap initial message sync.

rust_commands.name: messages_list
rust_commands.purpose: List recent messages from a specified chat with filtering by time, sender, media type, and order.

rust_commands.name: send
rust_commands.purpose: Send text, quoted replies, or media files with captions, MIME override, and custom filenames—but fails if sync is not running due to LID cache dependency.

rust_commands.name: sync
rust_commands.purpose: Run non-interactive sync to capture message history continuously or once; required for reliable message sending.

mvp_plan: week 1: Enable basic message listing and search by chat/time
week 1: Implement auth flow with QR display and initial sync
week 1: Set up SQLite store with FTS5 support and fallback to LIKE
week 1: Support sending plain text messages
week 2: Add quoted reply and media sending with caption/filename override
week 2: Implement contact and group listing/refresh
week 2: Integrate background media download during sync
acceptance_tests: 1:1 chat messages appear split between @s.whatsapp.net and @lid JIDs, causing fragmented history.
After successful `auth`, running `sync --follow` captures incoming messages without re-authentication.
LID normalization works during initial sync (`auth`) but fails during live sync (`sync --once`).
Messages sent successfully may not be delivered if internal message lookup fails ('couldn't find message' error).
Sending a message fails with timeout if `sync` is not running, due to missing LID cache.
SQLite store is secured against path injection and null byte exploits as patched in v0.6.0.
